cases.description: compare two KPIs for one zone
turns: Compare EBITDA margin and organic revenue growth for North America in 2025
cases.reason: unavailable=False, answer='## North America 2025: EBITDA Margin vs Organic Revenue Growth\n\n| Quarter | EBITDA Margin | Organic '
answers:
## North America 2025: EBITDA Margin vs Organic Revenue Growth

| Quarter | EBITDA Margin | Organic Revenue Growth |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Q1 2025 | 32.3% | -4.7% |
| Q2 2025 | 35.7% | +2.2% |
| Q3 2025 | 35.1% | -0.7% |
| Q4 2025 | 28.0% | -1.0% |

**What the two metrics say together**

- **Margins were strong for most of the year, but growth was not.** EBITDA margin held in the 32–36% range through Q1–Q3 before falling to 28.0% in Q4. Organic revenue growth, by contrast, was negative in three of four quarters, with Q1 the clear low point at -4.7% and Q2 the only positive quarter at +2.2%.
- **The two series decouple in Q3.** Margin stayed near its peak (35.1%, essentially flat vs. Q2's 35.7%) while organic growth slipped back to -0.7%. That pattern suggests margin was being supported by something other than top-line expansion (e.g., cost or mix effects), not by volume/revenue momentum.
- **Q4 is the weak spot on both fronts.** Margin dropped 7.1 percentage points sequentially (35.1% → 28.0%) at the same time organic growth remained slightly negative (-1.0%). Q4 is the only quarter where the two metrics moved in the same adverse direction.
- **Q1 vs. Q2 is the mirror image.** The weakest growth quarter (-4.7%) still delivered a 32.3% margin, and the only growth quarter (+2.2%) also happened to be the margin peak. So the relationship between growth and margin is not consistent across the year.

**Caveat on full-year figures:** The evidence provides only quarterly data — no reported full-year 2025 aggregate for either metric. A simple arithmetic average of the four quarters would be roughly ~32.8% EBITDA margin and ~-1.1% organic revenue growth, but that is an approximation, not an official AB InBev full-year figure, and should not be treated as one.

**Follow-up suggestions**
- What drove the Q4 2025 margin step-down in North America (35.1% → 28.0%) — is there commentary on cost or mix in internal documents?
- How does North America's 2025 margin/growth profile compare with other zones (e.g., South America or EMEA) for the same quarters?

cases.description: compare a brand's document-level context across two countries
turns: How does Corona's positioning differ between Mexico and other markets?
cases.reason: unavailable=False, answer='## Short answer\n\nBased on the retrieved evidence, the clearest documented difference is one of **bra'
answers:
## Short answer

Based on the retrieved evidence, the clearest documented difference is one of **brand scope and ownership**, not consumer positioning language: AB InBev's "Corona" megabrand is defined *excluding* Mexico, because a permanent license to the Corona/Modelo brand sits with Constellation Brands in that market [DOC-012]. Outside Mexico, Corona is counted and reported as one of AB InBev's four global "megabrands" (alongside Budweiser, Stella Artois and Michelob Ultra) and is therefore positioned as a **global, multi-country growth brand** rather than a Mexico-operated one.

## What the evidence actually supports

| Dimension | Mexico | Outside Mexico |
|---|---|---|
| Brand scope in AB InBev reporting | Excluded from the "Corona" megabrand definition; Corona/Modelo licensed to Constellation Brands [DOC-012] | Counted within AB InBev's megabrand portfolio (Budweiser, Corona, Stella Artois, Michelob Ultra) [DOC-012] |
| Growth role | Mexico volumes were **flat** in FY2025 [DOC-011] | Megabrands grew revenue **+4.6% in FY2024 and +4.1% in FY2025**, both ahead of total company revenue growth [DOC-012] |
| Financial reporting granularity | Not disclosed by country; sits inside the **Middle Americas** zone (per stated data limitation) | Tracked at megabrand level, not by individual market |

So the practical positioning split is: in Mexico, Corona is part of a **licensed portfolio** and Mexico volumes were flat [DOC-011]; internationally, AB InBev manages and markets Corona as a **premium global megabrand** that has been outgrowing the company average [DOC-012].

## Caveats — please read

- **The key sentence is truncated.** DOC-012 reads "Corona (outside Mexico, where Constellation Brands holds a permanent license to the Corona/Modelo brand…" and cuts off mid-clause. I've reported it as written, but the full filing should be checked before quoting it externally — the geographic scope of the license arrangement is exactly the kind of detail that a truncated snippet can distort.
- **No positioning narrative was retrieved.** The evidence contains no brand-positioning or consumer-messaging text (e.g. premium/import cues, target occasions, price tier) for either Mexico or other markets. If that's what you need, this evidence set does not answer it.
- **No country-level financials.** AB InBev does not publicly disclose structured financials by country [per stated limitation]. The nearest proxy is the **Middle Americas** zone, which includes Mexico — Q4 2025 revenue $4,927M (organic +5.9%), volume 39,672K hL, normalized EBITDA margin 50.9% [DOC-008], versus Q4 2024 revenue $4,395M (organic +6.6%), volume 38,907K hL, margin 50.7% [DOC-004]. Note these are *zone* figures and cannot be attributed to Corona or to Mexico alone.
- Competitor brand data (Heineken, Constellation Brands, etc.) is not maintained in queryable form in this build [DOC-014], so no benchmarking of Corona against rivals in either market is possible from this evidence.

## Worth checking next

- How did the **Middle Americas zone** (Mexico's reporting home) perform for the full FY2025, not just Q4, versus FY2024?
- How did Corona's growth compare with the other megabrands — Budweiser, Stella Artois and Michelob Ultra — in FY2025?
assumptions: AB InBev doesn't publicly disclose structured financials by country; showing the **Middle Americas** zone (which includes Mexico) instead, plus any Mexico-specific commentary found in the documents.
